title: Process listing fails when a process exits during scanning
body:
Fixes #186500

## Problem

On Linux, opening the process explorer (or anything that calls `listProcesses`) can fail with **"Listing processes failed"** whenever a short-lived process happens to exit while the list is being built. The reported error is `cat: /proc/<pid>/stat: No such file or directory`.

## Root cause

When GNU `ps` is unavailable, we fall back to `vs/base/node/ps.sh`, which enumerates numeric entries under `/proc` and then reads each process's `stat`, `cmdline`, etc. A process can exit at any point between enumeration and those reads:

- the `ls -d [0-9]*` enumeration itself races with process exit (`ls: cannot access '<pid>': No such file or directory`),
- the per-pid reads race too (`cat: /proc/<pid>/stat: No such file or directory` from `awk` reading `stat`, or errors from the `cmdline` redirection).

Any of these writes to stderr. `listProcesses()` in `ps.ts` treats **any** stderr output as total failure and rejects, so one vanished process out of hundreds kills the entire listing for the user.

## Fix

Every access to a process's files in `ps.sh` can race against that process exiting, so this change suppresses errors from those accesses and handles the vanished process gracefully:

- `2>/dev/null` on the `/proc` enumeration and on each per-pid read,
- an emptiness guard on the resident-set-size value so a failed `stat` read reports `0.0` memory instead of injecting an empty operand into the shell arithmetic (which would itself print an error),
- a comment explaining why the suppression is correct here.

The rest of the pipeline is unchanged: processes that still exist produce exactly the same output as before.

## Testing

- New regression suite in `src/vs/base/test/node/ps.test.ts`: spawns short-lived background processes while repeatedly executing the real `ps.sh`, asserts stderr stays empty across multiple rounds, with a quiet-system baseline control first. It is gated to run only where `/proc` exists (skipped elsewhere).
- Reproduced the bug deterministically before the fix on a real Linux environment (WSL2): under churn, **10/10** measurement rounds produced race stderr (`ls: cannot access '<pid>'` / `cat: /proc/<pid>/stat` shapes), while the quiet-system baseline was clean - proving the failures are churn-induced.
- After the fix: repeated measurement rounds under sustained identical churn produced **zero stderr**, and a quiet-system output-equivalence check (original vs fixed script, excluding the checker's own transient processes) showed identical listings.
- `npm run transpile-client` passes; targeted ESLint on the changed test file is clean; unit run of `Process Utils` shows the existing regex tests passing and the new Linux-gated suite correctly *pending* on Windows.

## Potential risks

- Low: behavior changes are confined to the fallback shell script used on Linux when `ps` is missing, plus the new test. Output shape for live processes is unchanged (verified by the equivalence check), so parsing in `parsePsOutput` is unaffected.
- A process that exits mid-scan now appears with placeholder values (or is omitted by the enumeration filter) instead of failing the whole listing - that degraded-but-useful row is strictly better than the current total failure, and matches what `ps` itself does under the same conditions.
- Not verified on macOS (unchanged code path) or inside a packaged VS Code client; the Linux verification was done against the real script in a real `/proc` environment rather than through the full app UI.

title: agentHost: Discover remote Copilot sessions
Cancelling cells of a closed notebook throws instead of being ignored
body:
Fixes #187448

## Problem

Cell cancellation is sent from the renderer to the extension host, but by the time it arrives the notebook document can already be gone - the notebook was closed, or the extension host restarted while cancellation was in flight. The lookup then throws `NO notebook document for 'file:///...'` straight out of the RPC dispatcher (`$cancelCells` -> `getNotebookDocument`), which is a long-running top error-telemetry bucket and interrupts whatever else the extension host was doing.

## Root cause

`$cancelCells` uses the strict overload of `getNotebookDocument` and has no guard for a missing document, unlike the kernel-lookup right above it in the same method which already handles a disposed kernel gracefully.

## Fix

`$cancelCells` now looks the document up in relaxed mode and returns silently when it is gone - there is nothing left to cancel. The existing behavior for live notebooks is unchanged.

## Testing

New test in `extHostNotebookKernel.test.ts`: cancelling cells of an unknown notebook URI is ignored (no throw, no interrupt call), and cancelling cells of a live notebook still reaches the interrupt handler.

Before the fix, the new test fails with exactly the production error: `Error: NO notebook document for 'file:///path/to/gone.ipynb'`. After: passing. Full `NotebookKernel` suite: 19 passing. `npm run typecheck-client` clean, ESLint clean on both changed files.

## Potential risks

None known - the only behavior change is for documents that no longer exist, where the previous behavior was an unhandled throw.

title: Web Agents omits remote SDK sessions as unsupported or missing client name

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
remote agent sessions are filtered out as 'external'.

The Agent Host log confirms that discovery can enumerate the sessions, but classification drops them: (this was before the default external setting was changed to `recent`)

```text
[Copilot] Listed 2 SDK session(s) for discoverable chats
[Copilot] Chat discovery: 2 SDK session(s) -> 0 external, ... 2 with unsupported or missing client name ...
[AgentService] listSessions computed 0 of 0 session(s) for mode 'none'
```

repro steps
1. open a dev box use the agents window to create more than two sessions
2. click the "Allow connections from other machines..." button above the sessions list
3. go to insider.vscode.dev and connect to that tunnel, or connect to remote agent host from a different agents window.

:bug: only the 2 most recent sessions are shown


from copilot:

## Most likely cause

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331187

External chat discovery in `copilotAgent.ts` currently does this for every non-adoptable session:

```ts
const clientName = s.isRemote ? undefined : s.clientName;
if (clientName === undefined || !COPILOT_EXTERNAL_SESSION_CLIENT_NAMES.has(clientName)) {
    unsupportedClientName++;
    return undefined;
}
```

The supported client names are `github/cli` and `github/autopilot`.

As a result, a session with `isRemote: true` is treated as if its client name were missing, even when the persisted client name identifies a supported producer. Sessions created by another remote/runtime client may likewise be excluded if that producer omits `clientName` or uses a different value.

This explains why the SDK catalog contains the sessions while the Web Agents session list is empty.

## Suggested change

Represent and validate remote provenance explicitly instead of unconditionally discarding `clientName` when `isRemote` is true. For example:

1. Preserve the SDK-provided client name for remote sessions.
2. Add an explicit allowlist/classification path for supported remote session producers.
3. Continue requiring a working directory, repository metadata, and the existing recency window.
4. Log `isRemote`, sanitized client provenance, and the specific rejection category separately so a remote-provenance rejection is not reported as a missing client name.

If remote sessions must remain excluded for trust or resume-safety reasons, the UI or logs should identify that constraint directly rather than classifying them as an unsupported/missing client name.

title: Notebooks of a view type break when their serializer registers twice
body:
Fixes #174051

## Problem

After a crash or restart of the extension host, an extension that provides a notebook serializer (for example the `sql-book` provider from the issue) registers again, but the stale registration from the previous extension host is sometimes still present. Registration then throws `notebook provider for viewtype 'X' already exists` out of the RPC dispatcher, the serializer never becomes active, and every notebook of that view type fails to open until the window is reloaded. This has been one of the top error-telemetry buckets for years.

## Root cause

`NotebookService._registerProviderData` treats an existing entry for the same view type as a hard error. That is correct for two different extensions fighting over one view type, but wrong when the *same* registration arrives again after an extension host restart and the old disposable was not run in time.

## Fix

Registering now replaces the existing entry instead of throwing:

- the fresh serializer takes effect immediately, so notebooks of the view type keep working across extension host restarts
- when the replacement switches extensions, that is logged as a warning (`ILogService`), since it indicates two extensions claiming the same type
- disposing a stale registration no longer removes the fresh entry — a registration only removes itself while it is still the current one
- the replace logic lives in a small exported helper (`registerProviderData`) so it can be unit tested without instantiating the service (its constructor claims process-global extension points)

## Testing

New test in `notebookServiceImpl.test.ts`: re-registering replaces the entry, reports the replaced extension id, stale disposal does not remove the fresh registration, and disposing the current one cleans up.

Before the fix, the equivalent call sequence fails with exactly the production error: `Error: notebook provider for viewtype 'sql-book' already exists`. After: passing. Also ran the neighboring `NotebookProviderInfoStore` suite (passing), `npm run typecheck-client` (clean) and ESLint on the changed files (clean).

## Potential risks

- Extensions that relied on the throw to detect duplicate view types will no longer see an error; the last registration wins, which matches what users expect (the newly activated extension works).

title: Fix element picker with mobile emulation
body: ## Summary Fix element picking under Mobile Emulation while preserving the emulated mobile presentation and page input behavior. Fixes #332182 ## Root Cause Mobile Emulation converts mouse input into touch input. Before contact begins, this conversion suppresses the pointer movement events that the element picker uses for hover highlighting. Disabling Mobile Emulation is not a suitable workaround because it can change the responsive layout and the element being inspected. ## Implementation - temporarily stop mouse-to-touch conversion while element selection is active - keep touch capability, the emulated viewport, and `(pointer: coarse)` active - keep the regular cursor for accurate element selection - suppress mouse-origin hover events while Mobile Emulation is active so picker activation and shutdown do not change page event delivery - restore mouse-to-touch conversion when element selection stops - synchronize suppression when Mobile Emulation changes and for newly adopted frames ## Scope and Risk The behavior change is limited to the Integrated Browser's Mobile Emulation and element picker. Normal Mobile Emulation continues converting mouse input into touch input before selection starts and after it stops. Desktop input behavior remains unchanged. ## Testing - `npm run transpile-client` - `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-browser/preload-browserView.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserView.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserViewEmulator.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserViewFrameInspector.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserViewInspector.ts` - `git diff --check` - manually verified: - hover highlighting and rectangle selection under Mobile Emulation - all 19 monitored page event counters remain unchanged through hover, drag release, picker shutdown, and subsequent mouse movement - Mobile Emulation without the picker delivers Pointer and Touch events while Mouse events remain suppressed - returning to Desktop emulation restores normal Pointer and Mouse event delivery - Desktop to Mobile and Mobile to Desktop transitions while the picker remains active ## Reproduction Before the Fix With Mobile Emulation enabled, the circular touch cursor moves, but the element highlight does not follow the pointer.

title: Fix unfolding folded regions on Android vscode.dev
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/292361

## Problem
On **vscode.dev in Android Chrome**, folding a region works, but tapping the same region to unfold does not. The reporter’s video shows the inline fold placeholder (`...`), not only the gutter chevron.

This is a high-impact editor-folding bug: once a region is collapsed on a phone, there is no reliable way to get that code back without a reload or a desktop client. I prioritized it because the folding *model* is fine — the failure is in touch input — so a small, targeted fix restores a basic editing action on the web.

## Root cause
Two cooperating input bugs on Android phones (`PointerEventHandler` is used when `isIOS || isAndroid` and pointer events exist):

1. **Inline `...` placeholder (primary, matches the issue video)**  
   Gesture is registered only on `linesContentDomNode`. A tap on `...` is handled as a Gesture `Tap`, which calls `preventDefault()` and originally dispatched with `leftButton: false`. `FoldingController.onEditorMouseDown` returned immediately unless the event had a left or middle button, so the unfold path never ran.

2. **Duplicate `mouseup` on the gutter**  
   `PointerEventHandler` skipped touch `pointerdown` but still handled touch `pointerup`. Android Chrome also fires a compatibility `mouseup`. After unfold, the same icon is still under the finger, so the second `mouseup` immediately re-folded the region.

Android tablets were also left on `TouchHandler`, which never forwarded taps to folding contributions at all.

## What changed
- **`pointerHandler.ts`**: emit mouse down/up from Gesture taps (`PointerEventHandler` and `TouchHandler`) so folding sees the tap; ignore touch `pointerup` as well as `pointerdown`; use the pointer+gesture path on all Android devices, not only phones (`isMobile`).
- **`folding.ts`**: accept Gesture-shaped taps (`leftButton: false`) on `CONTENT_TEXT` (the `...` placeholder) and `CONTENT_EMPTY` (when `unfoldOnClickAfterEndOfLine` is on); clear `mouseDownInfo` after a successful toggle so a duplicate `mouseup` cannot toggle again.
- **`folding.test.ts`**: regression tests for duplicate gutter `mouseup`, placeholder tap unfold, and empty-content tap unfold.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run eslint` on the three changed files
- [x] `npm run typecheck-client`
- [x] `npm run compile-client` and `npm run compile-web` (0 errors)
- [x] Chromium folding unit tests, including the new `#292361` cases (3 passing in `folding.test.ts`; existing folding suites still green)
- [x] Manual: vscode.dev / Android Chrome — open a file, fold via gutter, tap `...` to unfold; fold/unfold again and confirm it does not snap back
- [x] Manual: gutter fold/unfold still works on desktop mouse

title: Restore persisted platform root config on agent host startup
body:
## Problem

The Agents window UI showed `chat.agentSessions.showExternal` as **Last 30 Days** while the agent host logged `showExternalSessions: 'none'` and hid external sessions.

`persistRootConfig` writes the whole root value bag to `agent-host-config.json`, but `_loadPersistedRootConfig` only restored five schema groups — customization, sandbox, copilotCli, agentMerge and proxy. Every `platformRootSchema` key was dropped on load, and [`AgentHostStateManager`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts) seeds only `permissions` and `telemetryLevel`, so those keys were genuinely absent from root config until a window connected and re-pushed them.

The host reads several of them before that happens, so they silently fell back to schema defaults.

## Evidence

From an `ah-logs` bundle, the `initialize` response carrying the host's cold-start root snapshot:

| Path in root-state snapshot | Present? |
| --- | --- |
| `config.schema.properties.showExternalSessions` | yes |
| `config.values.showExternalSessions` | **no** |

…even though `agent-host-config.json` on disk did contain `"showExternalSessions"`. A second window's `initialize` 48s later *does* carry the value — only because the first window had already re-pushed it.

The resulting sequence:

```
11:44:01  root/configChanged … "showExternalSessions":"none"
11:45:03  listSessions hid 48 of 394 session(s) (showExternalSessions: 'none')
11:46:32  showExternalSessions changed 'none' -> 'recent'; queueing session list reconciliation
```

`_getExternalSessionsMode()` fell through to `?? AgentHostExternalSessionsMode.None`, so the first catalog pass and the initial external-session reconciliation both ran under `none`.

## Impact beyond the reported symptom

The same gap affected every other `platformRootSchema` key read before a client connects:

- `codexAgentEnabled` — read during provider registration in `agentHostMain.ts` / `agentHostServerMain.ts`, so Codex could fail to register on a cold start
- `migrateLegacyCopilotCliEnabled` — read early in `listSessions`
- `editTelemetryEnabled`
- hand-edited values in a remote `agent-host-config.json`, which operators expect to be authoritative

## Fix

Restore the platform-owned keys alongside the other schema groups, via `platformRootSchema.validateOrDefault` so malformed entries still fall back to defaults rather than being loaded verbatim.

Root `permissions` stays excluded: it mirrors the connected client's managed settings, so reviving a previous run's value could re-grant an allow rule that has since been revoked. It is left for the client to republish.

## Testing

Added a round-trip test in `agentConfigurationService.test.ts` that persists `last30Days` plus a permissions rule, constructs a fresh service against the same file, and asserts the mode survives the restart while permissions do not.

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- New test passes
- Full node unit suite: same pre-existing Windows failures (`SessionPermissionManager` path tests, `AgentHostDebugLogsCollector`) before and after the change

title: sessions: hide external Recent sessions superseded by newer local ones
body:
Adjusts the `Recent` external-sessions mode so it stops surfacing external sessions the user has clearly moved on from.

## What changed

`Recent` still shows the 2 most recently updated external sessions from the last 7 days, but now hides any of them that **2 locally created sessions have started after its last update**.

Implemented in `_getRecentSessionKeys` via a single cutoff — the start time of the 2nd-newest local session. An external session is dropped when its `modifiedTime` predates that cutoff:

| Local sessions | 10am external | 4pm external |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none after 10am | shown | shown |
| one at 11am | shown | shown |
| 11am + 5pm | **hidden** | shown |
| 5pm + 5pm | **hidden** | **hidden** |

## Why the cutoff is snapshotted

Sending a first message is what materializes a local session, so a cutoff derived on every listing would rotate an external row out of the list while the user is looking at it. `_getRecentSupersedingCutoff` therefore snapshots the value on the first `Recent` listing and refreshes it only when the external-sessions mode changes.

The existing external-session reconciliation listener is untouched, so the top-2 selection still rotates when external sessions are discovered or updated.

## Notes for reviewers

- Three setting/banner strings now read "up to the 2 most recently updated…" instead of promising exactly 2.
- Two new tests in `agentService.test.ts`: the four scenarios above, and one asserting the visible set stays put after two local sessions appear but updates once the mode changes.
- Validation: `npm run typecheck-client` clean, eslint clean on changed files, full `agentService.test.js` suite passes (357 passing), sessions banner test passes. `npm run hygiene` fails in this worktree on a pre-existing doubled-drive-letter path bug (`C:\C:\...\remote\package.json`), unrelated to these changes.

title: File watcher silently stops working when watched folder is renamed
body:
Fixes #309241

## Problem

When you rename or move a folder that is being watched recursively from outside the workspace, the file watcher never tells anyone. On Windows and macOS the underlying watcher handle survives the rename, so no events arrive at all: no `onDidDelete` for the base folder, and every later change inside the renamed folder goes unnoticed. The same rename inside the workspace behaves correctly, which is exactly the inconsistency reported in #309241.

I reproduced this on current main against the real `ParcelWatcher` backend: after renaming the watched root, the watcher delivered zero events, fired no fail signal, and stayed silent even for new files created inside the renamed folder.

## Root cause

`ParcelWatcher` only reacts to a lost watch path when an explicit `DELETED` event for the root arrives (`filterEvents` → `rootDeleted`). A rename produces no such event, so the existing recovery machinery in `BaseWatcher` (suspend/resume) never kicks in, and clients are left watching a ghost.

## Fix

This change adds a small periodic existence check on the watched root to `startWatching()`. If the root disappears without any event having been received, we synthesize the root `DELETED` event and run it through the exact same pipeline as a real deletion (`handleParcelEvents` → fail → suspend/resume). That means:

- clients now get `onDidDelete` for the renamed base folder
- the watcher enters suspend and automatically resumes when the path comes back
- polling watchers are untouched; Linux is unaffected because inotify already reports the rename as real events (and the new check backs off once the watcher has failed)

The check itself is one `fs.access` per watcher every 5 seconds (~0.05 ms per call measured), in line with the existing suspended-request monitoring cadence.

## Testing

- Added a regression test to the existing parcel watcher suite: `renaming watched path emits watcher fail and delete event if correlated`
- Verified it **fails before** the fix (timeout waiting for events) and **passes after** it
- Full parcel suite: 29 passing before and after, only pre-existing flaky failures unchanged
- Broader unit suite: 52 failures before the change on this machine, 52 identical failures after (all unrelated `agentHost`/environment issues)
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes; ESLint clean on both changed files

## Potential risks

- macOS behavior is expected to mirror Windows (FSEvents also keeps handles alive across renames), but I could only verify Windows locally
- The synthetic delete can arrive up to ~5 s after the actual rename

title: Allow renaming or moving a project folder while persisting history for Copilot chats (re-file of #313970)
body:
This supersedes #313970, which was closed by the backlog-candidate process after it did not reach 20 community upvotes in 60 days. The need has not gone away, and if anything has grown with agentic workflows, so I am re-filing with the additional feedback that accumulated there.

## Problem

As a user, I often don't know upfront where a project folder will finally live. I might start working in a folder on the Desktop and move it later, or restructure existing folders. Currently, moving or renaming a project folder loses the association to its Copilot chat/session history (related: local history #152415, workspace-scoped storage #257143).

Losing session history this way actively discourages healthy project restructuring, and with more and more agentic coding (including the Agents window), long-lived session history attached to a project keeps getting more valuable.

## What would help

1. **Supported rename/move**: a context-menu action or command ("Move/Rename project folder") that relocates the folder and transparently re-maps existing Copilot chat sessions to the new location.
2. **Folder identity instead of absolute paths**: identify a project by content fingerprint or an ID stored inside the folder, so sessions can be re-associated after a move, and "orphaned" sessions can be offered for re-linking.
3. **Workspace-detached history** (from @Metadorius on #313970): chats stored independently of a single workspaceStorage bucket and filtered by "last workspace used in", so they remain visible and continuable from other windows/locations.
4. **Machine-portable history** (from @gidimiz-ST on #313970): either bind history to project identity rather than machine-local storage, or provide an official export/import so the same repo on another PC can pick up prior conversations.

## Related

- Previous attempt: #313970 (closed after upvote window; contains additional discussion)
- Older related reports: #152415, #257143
- Parallel requests in other agent tools, which already track the same need:
  - Codex: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15347 (assigned)
  - Claude Code: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/88903
  - OpenCode: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/44256

Consistent behavior across these tools would remove a recurring pain point for users who work with several agents on the same projects.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. This occurs on the hosted `vscode.dev/agents` page before GitHub Enterprise authentication completes.

- VS Code Version: Current production build served by `https://vscode.dev/agents` on 2026-08-23
- OS Version: Android 16, OnePlus 15
- Browsers: Chrome and the OnePlus built-in browser
- On-screen keyboards: Microsoft SwiftKey and Gboard
- Feature: Agents page, GitHub Enterprise Cloud sign-in

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open `https://vscode.dev/agents` on Android.
2. Start sign-in for a GitHub Enterprise Cloud account.
3. Enter a valid GHE.com hostname, such as `company.ghe.com`, in the prompt "What is your GHE.com instance?"
4. Press the on-screen keyboard Enter, Done, or checkmark action.
5. Repeat with another Android keyboard and browser.

Expected behavior:

The input is accepted and the GitHub Enterprise authentication flow continues.

Actual behavior:

Nothing happens. The input remains open and authentication cannot continue. The same GHE.com hostname works from a PC browser.

The problem reproduces with both SwiftKey and Gboard, and with both Chrome and the OnePlus built-in browser. This makes the GitHub Enterprise sign-in flow unusable from the Android Agents page.

Related reports:

- #280016 reported that Enter did not submit `showInputBox` prompts in VS Code Web. It was closed after the requested diagnostics arrived after the automatic closure.
- #302363 tracks the broader need for a mobile-optimized Agent Mode view.

The real enterprise hostname is redacted because this is a public issue. A screenshot is available, but it contains the hostname and machine name.

title: agentHost: add a chat contribution model for cross-cutting behavior
body:
Introduces a registry-driven contribution model for the agent host so cross-cutting behavior lives in self-contained modules instead of branches inlined in `AgentSideEffects` and `AgentService`.

The goal is that a feature which touches several points in the turn lifecycle (contribute a command, add context on the way out, strip it from rendered history) can be written once, in one folder, rather than as separate branchy code in each place.

## Hooks

| Hook | Fires |
|---|---|
| `onTurnEnd` | every terminal outcome, discriminated by a `TurnEndReason` union |
| `contributeSend` | before a turn is sent; results concatenated in `order` |
| `onHydrateTurns` | whole restored turn list, as a pipeline |
| `onAction` | client dispatched actions |
| `onUserMessage` | a user message admitted on the direct path |

## Contributions

`queueDrain`, `persistedTurnUsage`, `sessionTitle`, `checkpointAndChangeset`, `markdownPlanRichLinks`, `markUnread`, `githubReferences`, `chatSurface`, `worktreeAnnouncement`, `artifactTools`.

Each lives in its own subfolder and is registered explicitly in `createAgentService` from one shared list, mirroring `IAgentHostChangesetOperationService`. Sequencing comes from an explicit `order`; registration order is only a tiebreak.

## Supporting work

- A per-contribution context with chat and session scoped mementos, evicted centrally when a chat or session is disposed. This replaces the pattern of each collaborator keeping its own URI keyed map with its own cleanup path, and let `clearQueuedMessageSenders` and both of its call sites be deleted.
- Several collaborators that `AgentSideEffects` constructed privately are now services owned by the composition root: the session title controller, telemetry reporter, turn tracker, and local command dispatcher.
- The bespoke host bridge that existed because these were not injectable is down from seven members to two: `hostLaunchKind` and `sendTurnMessage`.

## Behavior

Behavior preserving throughout. The existing `agentSideEffects` suite is unchanged and still passes, which is the proof for each extraction. Full agent host suite after merging `main`: 6069 passing, 70 pending, 0 failing (`main` alone is 6037 passing).

## Known gaps, recorded in `chatContributions/TODO.md`

- The queued admission path does not attach GitHub references from a user message, while the direct path does. This predates the PR; it closes when turn admission is unified.
- Direct and queued admission now duplicate local command interception, title seeding, agent lookup, and telemetry setup. That duplication was previously hidden behind a bridge method; making it visible is deliberate, and `onIncomingRequest` removes it.

## Not done yet

- `onIncomingRequest` to unify turn admission, retire `sendTurnMessage`, and fold in the local command registry.
- Migrating the side chat (`/btw`) feature onto `contributeSend` plus `onHydrateTurns`, which should delete its per harness wiring in the Copilot and Claude agents and give Codex support by deletion.

## Merge status

`origin/main` is merged in. Upstream had changed `AgentHostTurnTracker.turnStarted` to take the agent object plus a trailing client id, and moved the tracker to `createInstance`; both call sites this PR created were updated, and the queued path passes its own sender client id.

title: `run_in_terminal` automatically embeds image paths from stdout without an aggregate limit, causing renderer OOM
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.62.0
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0 Stable (`110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419`)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9168, x64
- Feature: Agent mode
- Selected model: GPT 5.6
- Logs: Not attached. The cause is directly reproducible and the relevant implementation is identified below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a workspace containing many image files smaller than 5 MiB.
2. Start an Agent chat with the built-in terminal tool enabled.
3. Have the agent run a command that prints path-like image filenames, such as `git status --short --untracked-files=all`.
4. Continue using the task or reopen it and observe rapidly increasing renderer memory.

The built-in `run_in_terminal` tool scans the full terminal output for paths ending in PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, or BMP. It resolves every matching path relative to the terminal working directory, reads the file, and appends its bytes to the tool result.

The relevant result path is effectively:

```js
const cwd = await terminal.instance.getCwdResource();
const images = await this._extractImagesFromOutput(fullRawOutput, cwd);

return {
  content: [
    { kind: "text", value: processedText },
    ...images
  ]
};
```

`_extractImagesFromOutput` enforces a 5 MiB per-file limit but has no image-count or aggregate-byte limit. It also receives the full raw output, so terminal output truncation and `chat.tools.terminal.outputCompaction` do not prevent the issue.

This means commands such as `git status`, `find`, recursive directory listings, asset inventories, and build reports can unintentionally attach every image path they print. The image bytes are subsequently serialized as base64 into the task state and duplicated between tool-result metadata and response details.

In my reproduction:

- Approximately 120 KiB of terminal text produced 72 embedded image parts.
- One serialized terminal result grew to approximately 33.5 MiB.
- The active task exceeded 500 MiB on disk.
- Reopening or rendering the task expanded memory usage until the renderer reached its heap limit and crashed with OOM.

Expected behavior:

Terminal stdout should be returned as text. Paths printed by arbitrary commands should not be dereferenced and attached automatically. Images should only be loaded following an explicit image-view request.

At minimum, please add an option such as:

```json
"chat.tools.terminal.extractImagesFromOutput": false
```

Image extraction should preferably default to disabled. If retained, it should have conservative image-count and aggregate-byte limits and should only inspect output retained after compaction.

title: Code, on Linux, is bleeding internal env vars into delve sessions.
body:
Type: Bug What you are seeing is an internal Electron/VS Code architecture leak, rather than an OS bug.What is actually happeningVS Code is built on Electron, which uses the Chromium engine underneath. To keep the UI fast, VS Code offloads work to separate background utility worker processes. In your case, the process handling the built-in Markdown Language Features extension is running inside a background NodeJS worker.When the VS Code compilation team builds the production version of VS Code, they intentionally pass DEBUG=release directly to their internal JavaScript toolchains and extension builds (like the Markdown server) to disable development logs, enable minification, and maximize performance.Why Delve is inheriting itNormally, an extension's environment is sandboxed. However, because of the way VS Code launches debugger sidecars (like Delve for Go), Delve is fork-spawned as a child process of the broad VS Code Extension Host layer.Instead of Delve cleanly inheriting just your system's global environment variables, it is accidentally picking up the internal DEBUG=release flag that the VS Code core engine injected into its extension worker runtime environment. body:
Stacked on #332100. Adds `sessionTypeSelectionReason` to `interactiveSessionProviderInvoked` so harness adoption can be attributed to explicit selection, workspace constraints, remembered/current state, Copilot preference, or the computed default. Threads the creation reason through sidebar/editor creation, clear, provider selection, forks, split/duplicate, and untitled remote-session materialization while keeping it out of restored editor state. | Property | What it is | Values and meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `sessionTypeSelectionReason` | The highest-precedence signal that determined the session type when the session was created. | `explicitOverride`: a caller or user explicitly chose the type.
`virtualWorkspace`: the session type was automatically set to Local because the chat was opened in a virtual workspace.
`rememberedSelection`: the user's last usable selection was restored.
`currentSession`: the current session's usable type was preserved, including clear, fork, and split/duplicate flows.
`copilotPreference`: the Copilot harness preference replaced an otherwise local current session.

title: Fix Markdown token cache invalidation for typographer
body:
## Summary

Changing the `markdown.preview.typographer` setting previously refreshed the preview, but could reuse Markdown tokens parsed under the old option. An unchanged document could therefore keep straight quotes, dashes, ellipses, and symbol substitutions until another action forced it to parse again.

This change includes `typographer` in the token cache key. A configuration change now reparses the document, while repeated renders of the same document instance and version continue to reuse cached tokens.

## Regression Coverage

The new tests establish the cache contract:

- The same document instance and version parses once, verified with a Markdown-It core-rule counter.
- Changing a document's version invalidates tokens and renders its updated content.
- Changing `markdown.preview.typographer` invalidates tokens and applies typographic substitutions.

The test engine accepts an isolated Markdown-It plugin contribution solely to make parsing observable in the cache-hit test; production contribution handling is unchanged, and the existing test path still uses empty contributions. The version test uses a mutable `ITextDocument` fake because `InMemoryDocument` deliberately keeps text and version immutable. This preserves document identity while exercising version invalidation directly.

## Manual Verification

1. Run the development build and open a Markdown file containing:

   ```md
   "Hello..." -- it's 50 (c)
   ```

2. Set `markdown.preview.typographer` to `false` and run **Markdown: Open Preview to the Side**.
3. Without editing the file, set `markdown.preview.typographer` to `true`.
4. Confirm the existing preview updates to `“Hello…” – it’s 50 ©`.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp -- compile-extension:markdown-language-features`
- `npm run test-extension -- -l markdown-language-features --grep "markdown.engine" --fail-zero` (12 passing)

title: New chats remain stuck in Agent Host after switching back to Local Chat due to persisted chat.userSelectedSessionType
body:
### Problem

After Agent Host / Copilot CLI has been selected once, VS Code can persist:

```text
chat.userSelectedSessionType = agent-host-copilotcli
```

in:

```text
User/globalStorage/state.vscdb
```

After changing the chat configuration back to Local / Extension Host and fully restarting VS Code, newly created Agent chats still open as Agent Host sessions.

Third-party language models remain correctly registered and visible in normal Chat / Manage Models:

```text
availableModels="unify-chat-provider/...many models...,copilot/auto"
```

But each newly created Agent chat is still routed to:

```text
sessionKey="agent-host-copilotcli"
modelTarget="agent-host-copilotcli"
availableModels="agent-host-copilotcli:auto"
```

So the user can change the relevant Local / Agent Host settings, restart VS Code, and still be effectively trapped in the previously selected Agent Host session type for new chats.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Agent Host / Copilot CLI so that VS Code persists `chat.userSelectedSessionType=agent-host-copilotcli`.
2. Change the chat configuration back to prefer / enable the Local / Extension Host path.
3. Fully restart VS Code.
4. Create a new Agent chat.
5. Observe that the new session is still created as `agent-host-copilotcli`.

### Expected behavior

Changing the harness configuration back to Local / Extension Host should affect newly created chats after restart.

The user should be able to leave Agent Host through supported settings / UI without manually editing VS Code's internal state database.

### Actual behavior

The persisted `chat.userSelectedSessionType` continues to win, so new chats remain on `agent-host-copilotcli` even after explicitly switching the relevant settings back to Local.

For example, the behavior persisted with:

```json
"chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness": false,
"chat.defaultToCopilotHarness": false,
"chat.editor.localAgent.enabled": true,
"chat.editor.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost": false
```

### Investigation

I found the persisted value in `User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`.

Looking at the VS Code 1.134 workbench code, `chat.userSelectedSessionType` is considered before the default harness selection. This matches the observed behavior: while the persisted entry exists, it overrides the explicit Local harness configuration for new chats.

The strongest confirmation is that removing only this persisted entry changes the routing immediately after restart.

### Workaround

With VS Code fully closed, remove only:

```text
chat.userSelectedSessionType
```

from `User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`.

Before:

```text
chat.userSelectedSessionType = agent-host-copilotcli
```

After removing that single state entry and restarting VS Code:

```text
sessionKey=undefined
modelTarget=undefined
availableModels="unify-chat-provider/..."
```

New chats return to the Local / Extension Host path and the third-party models become selectable again.

### Environment

- VS Code: `1.134.0`
- OS: Windows 11 + Remote WSL2 (Ubuntu)

### Scope

This report is about VS Code's built-in chat session routing / persisted session-type state. A third-party language model provider made the symptom visible, but the persisted routing behavior itself is in VS Code core.

There also appears to be a separate Agent Host BYOK bridge issue where third-party models work in Local Chat but Agent Host exposes only `Auto`; that is already being discussed in #326344.

This issue is specifically about the persisted session-type selection preventing the user from returning to Local Chat even after changing the relevant configuration.

title: MSAL: stale session records in SecretStorage cause Settings Sync sign-out every ~1h
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (provider is the built-in `vscode.microsoft-authentication`)

- VS Code Version: 1.133.x and 1.134.0 (stable); `@azure/msal-node-extensions@5.3.2` per log
- OS Version: Windows 10 22H2 and Windows 11 (x64); macOS Sonoma 14.x (arm64)

Related: #242814 (same broker error code 3399614467; the `classic` workaround no longer exists), #291146, #291738 (same `tag_7cisv` on startup).

## Summary

Settings Sync with a **personal Microsoft account** signs out roughly 30–60 minutes after every login, on Windows and macOS alike, with both `microsoft-authentication.implementation: msal` and `msal-no-broker`.

Root cause, confirmed by inspecting SecretStorage and by the fix below: the extension's SecretStorage had accumulated **five session records for the same account** plus **two MSAL cache (PCA) entries in legacy and current key formats** for the same client ID. Interactive re-login adds a new session record but never removes the old ones or the legacy PCA cache. On the first silent refresh after the access token expires (~1h), `getAllSessionsForPca` ends up using a refresh token issued months earlier (2026-05-20 in my case); the server rejects it, the account is skipped, `getSessions` returns 0 sessions, and Settings Sync shows "Sign in to Sync Settings".

That stale token hit its 90-day inactivity limit on 2026-08-18, which is why the symptom appeared right after updating to 1.133 — the update itself looks coincidental. Accounts → Sign out does **not** remove the stale records. Deleting the extension's keys from `state.vscdb` does, and the account then stays signed in (verified on both OSes).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a personal MS account (`user@outlook.com`) for Settings Sync for several months across VS Code updates (so legacy cache keys exist).
2. Accounts menu → Sign out → Sign in again with the same account (Windows via WAM broker, or `msal-no-broker` on either OS).
3. Wait ~1 hour (access token expiry); the next Settings Sync interval triggers a silent refresh.
4. `Microsoft Authentication` output shows `failed to acquire token silently, skipping account` → `returned 0 session(s)`; the Settings Sync badge appears.
5. Repeat 2–4: every fresh login lasts ~1 hour.

## Evidence

### SecretStorage contents before the fix (Windows, `state.vscdb`)

```
sqlite3 state.vscdb "select key from ItemTable where key like '%microsoft-authentication%' or key like '%vscode.login%';"

secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"accounts-AzureCloud"}

secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"f8cdef31-a31e-4b4a-93e4-5f571e91255a/1:live.com:<puid>/377a0ad8-9152-471b-9357-de0b7a147179"}
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"f8cdef31-a31e-4b4a-93e4-5f571e91255a/1:live.com:<puid>/6747d3fa-2783-45e0-94a7-65a85ae1f799"}
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"f8cdef31-a31e-4b4a-93e4-5f571e91255a/1:live.com:<puid>/6d52d711-ff2e-4667-90e3-3fca041c8b60"}
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"f8cdef31-a31e-4b4a-93e4-5f571e91255a/1:live.com:<puid>/b90372be-f945-4a32-b2a3-d22868553025"}
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"f8cdef31-a31e-4b4a-93e4-5f571e91255a/1:live.com:<puid>/ce323329-f19b-41b2-94af-402bc3f141c2"}
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"microsoft.login.keylist"}
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"pca:aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56"}
secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"pca:{\"clientId\":\"aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56\",\"authority\":\"https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations\"}"}

```

Observations:
- **5 session records** for a single MSA (`1:live.com:<puid>`), one per past sign-in. None were removed by Accounts → Sign out.
- **2 PCA cache entries** for the same client ID: legacy `pca:<clientId>` and current `pca:{"clientId","authority"}`. The legacy cache was never deleted after the key format changed; this is the likely home of the 2026-05-20 refresh token.
- **2 account-list keys** (`accounts-AzureCloud` vs `accounts-AzureCloud-<clientId>-<authority>`), same pattern.
- `microsoft.login.keylist` is a leftover from the removed `classic` implementation.

### macOS, `msal-no-broker` — stale refresh token used minutes after a fresh login

```

2026-08-22 20:52:06.625 [info] [getAllSessionsForPca] [email offline_access openid profile] [user@outlook.com] failed to acquire token silently, skipping account {"errorCode":"invalid_grant","errorMessage":"AADSTS700082: The refresh token has expired due to inactivity. The token was issued on 2026-05-20T09:56:03.7597431Z and was inactive for 90.00:00:00. Trace ID: 25571394-87be-457b-98fb-4077380a8c00 Correlation ID: 17025c53-72ee-416b-ab28-f1ffd53d4896 Timestamp: 2026-08-22 11:52:10Z","subError":"bad_token","correlationId":"17025c53-72ee-416b-ab28-f1ffd53d4896","name":"InteractionRequiredAuthError","timestamp":"2026-08-22 11:52:10Z","traceId":"25571394-87be-457b-98fb-4077380a8c00","claims":"","errorNo":700082}
2026-08-22 20:52:06.626 [info] [getSessions] [email offline_access openid profile] returned 0 session(s)
```

### Windows, `msal` (native broker) — same account twice in WAM, then AADSTS9002313

Startup:

Silent acquire right after:
```
2026-08-22 18:32:52.097 [info] [getSessions] [email offline_access openid profile] starting

2026-08-22 18:32:52.646 [info] [getSessions] [email offline_access openid profile] returned 0 session(s)
2026-08-22 18:32:52.646 [info] [getSessions] [499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798/.default offline_access] starting
...
2026-08-22 18:32:53.107 [info] [getSessions] [499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798/.default offline_access] returned 0 session(s)
```

### After the workaround (macOS, `msal-no-broker`, ~1h after login) — refresh succeeds

```
2026-08-22 22:00:53.048 [info] [getSessions] [email offline_access openid profile] starting
2026-08-22 22:00:53.390 [info] [getSessions] [email offline_access openid profile] returned 1 session(s)
2026-08-22 22:00:53.402 [info] [getSessions] [499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798/.default offline_access] starting
2026-08-22 22:00:53.406 [info] [getSessions] [499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798/.default offline_access] returned 1 session(s)
```

Same result on Windows after applying the same steps with `msal-no-broker`.

## Expected behavior

- Interactive sign-in should replace (or invalidate) existing cached records for the same `home_account_id`, so a fresh login never falls back to an older refresh token.
- On startup the extension should migrate or delete legacy keys (`pca:<clientId>`, `accounts-AzureCloud`, `microsoft.login.keylist`) instead of leaving a second, stale cache that silent acquire can still read.
- When silent acquire fails with `bad_token` / `AADSTS700082` for one record, try the other records for the same account (or drop the dead one) instead of returning 0 sessions.
- Accounts menu → Sign out should actually purge the account's records from SecretStorage.

## Workaround (verified on both OSes)

Signing out from the Accounts menu is **not** enough. Delete the extension's SecretStorage keys manually, then sign in again (on Windows, also switch to `msal-no-broker`). Listing the keys first (as above) confirms you're affected: multiple `<tenant>/1:live.com:<puid>/<uuid>` session keys, or both `pca:` key formats present.

macOS — quit VS Code, then:
```sh
DB=~/Library/Application\ Support/Code/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb
cp "$DB" ~/state.vscdb.bak
sqlite3 "$DB" "select key from ItemTable where key like '%microsoft-authentication%' or key like '%vscode.login%';"
sqlite3 "$DB" "delete from ItemTable where key like '%microsoft-authentication%' or key like '%vscode.login%';"
```

Windows — quit VS Code, then (cmd):
```cmd
set DB=%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb
copy /y "%DB%" "%DB%.bak"
sqlite3 "%DB%" "select key from ItemTable where key like '%%microsoft-authentication%%' or key like '%%vscode.login%%';"
sqlite3 "%DB%" "delete from ItemTable where key like '%%microsoft-authentication%%' or key like '%%vscode.login%%';"
rd /s /q "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\TokenBroker\Cache"
```
and set `"microsoft-authentication.implementation": "msal-no-broker"`.

Relaunch and sign in once. The account now survives token refresh across multiple sync intervals on both machines.

## Notes

- In 2025, `classic` worked around #242814; that option has since been removed, so affected users currently have no setting-only workaround other than moving Settings Sync to a GitHub account.
- The Windows WAM path shows an additional problem (the same MSA present twice in WAM, once as the Windows sign-in account) that `msal-no-broker` sidesteps. Happy to collect more broker-specific logs if useful.

title: sessions: defer managed Changes tab reconciliation until working-set restore settles
body:
I generated this by scanning my logs, pls take if it's good/useful

---
🤖 

## Summary

Defer the single-pane managed Changes/Files tab reconciliation while a session working-set restore is in progress, then let the existing restore-end reconciliation apply the latest accumulated intent against the settled editor group.

This prevents the managed-tab coordinator from replacing a stale Changes tab concurrently with `IEditorGroupsService.applyWorkingSet`, which can dispose and recreate the editor group underneath that replacement.

## User-visible symptom and log evidence

While switching rapidly among recent Agent Host sessions in the Agents Window, the renderer repeatedly logged a canceled editor open immediately followed by a disposed scoped instantiation service:

```text
2026-08-21 18:34:57.934 [error] Canceled: Canceled
    at ...setInput
    at ...doOpenEditor
    at ...replaceEditors
    at ..._reconcileForeignChangesEditors
    at ..._reconcileCore
    at ..._reconcile
2026-08-21 18:34:57.934 [error] InstantiationService has been disposed: Error: InstantiationService has been disposed
    at ..._throwIfDisposed
    at ...createInstance
    at ...doInstantiateEditorPane
    at ...doCreateEditorPane
    at ...doShowError
    at ...replaceEditors
    at ..._reconcileForeignChangesEditors
```

I found 10 occurrences of `InstantiationService has been disposed` across recent Insiders sessions on August 19-21, all with the same managed-tab reconciliation path.

The second error is a consequence of the first: once the editor open is canceled, the editor pane attempts to show an error placeholder, but the old editor group's scoped instantiation service has already been disposed by the concurrent working-set replacement.

## Root cause

A session switch currently drives two related asynchronous paths:

1. `BaseLayoutController` applies the incoming session's editor working set under `_withSessionLayoutRestore(...)`.
2. `SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator` observes the active-session change and immediately queues an ambient managed-tab reconciliation.

The coordinator's `_reconcileForeignChangesEditors` can therefore call `group.replaceEditors(...)` for the incoming session's Changes tab while `applyWorkingSet(...)` is still replacing the outgoing editor group. The coordinator holds the group captured before the asynchronous operation settles, so its replacement can continue against a group whose scoped services have since been disposed.

The controller already exposes the intended synchronization boundary:

- `ctx.isRestoringSessionLayout` is true for the full asynchronous restore.
- `ctx.onDidEndSessionLayoutRestore` queues a reconciliation after the restore depth returns to zero.

The ambient session-change path was not respecting that boundary.

## Fix

`queueReconcile` still records the latest target, merges triggers for the same session, and advances the generation while restoration is active, but it does not start work against the transient editor group.

`_reconcile` also checks `isRestoringSessionLayout` before consuming `_pending`. This covers work that was queued immediately before a restore began but had not started yet.

When restoration settles, the existing `onDidEndSessionLayoutRestore` listener queues the final reconciliation. Because `_pending` was retained rather than discarded, trigger intent is preserved and merged with the restore-end trigger, while the newest generation continues to supersede stale queued work.

This is intentionally not an exception filter and does not suppress `Canceled` or disposed-service errors. It removes the ordering race that causes them.

## Regression coverage

The tests cover both sides of the scheduling boundary:

1. A restore is already active when a session switch requests reconciliation. The test verifies that `queueReconcile` retains the intent without scheduling replacement, then applies it after restore end.
2. A stale Changes replacement is queued first, and a gated restore starts before the sequencer callback runs. The test verifies that the `_reconcile` guard leaves the old tab untouched during restore and that the restore-end reconciliation performs exactly one replacement for the active session.

Together they verify that:

- no `replaceEditors` call occurs against a transient editor group;
- the pending target is retained across restoration;
- exactly one replacement occurs after restoration settles;
- the resulting Changes tab belongs to the active session.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- focused managed-tab session-switch tests: 8 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/test/browser/desktopSessionLayoutController.test.ts`
  - 141 passing
- pre-commit hygiene checks on all changed files
- `git diff --check`

## Reviewer context

@sandy081, this touches the generation/pending-intent logic introduced as part of the recent single-pane lifecycle stabilization work. The key behavior to review is that pending intents remain accumulated during restore and are consumed only by the already-existing restore-end reconciliation, rather than being dropped or run against the outgoing group.

title: agentHost: retire the optimistic turn start on the first backend action
body:
Fixes #332087

## Problem

`ChatStateSubscription` applies the client's own `chat/turnStarted` optimistically and holds it in `_pendingActions` until the backend echoes it back carrying the originating `clientSeq`. The agent host does not send that `clientSeq`, so the reconcile takes the non-origin branch and the pending start is never retired.

`_recomputeOptimistic()` rebuilds the optimistic state on every confirmed action by replaying the pending list over confirmed state:

```ts
let state = confirmed;
for (const pending of this._pendingActions) {
	state = chatReducer(state, pending.action as IProtocolChatAction, this._log);
}
```

Replaying a turn start resets `activeTurn` to a fresh empty turn, so `activeTurn.responseParts` reads as empty no matter how many deltas have already been folded into confirmed state. The UI reads the optimistic state, so `_observeTurn` resolves the turn by id but sees no parts, `autorunPerKeyedItem` never creates a per-part observer, and `_setupMarkdownPart` is never called. On completion the turn moves into `state.turns`, which a replayed turn start does not touch, and the whole reply appears in a single step.

Measured in a live window with the renderer instrumented, on a prompt producing about 2.4 KB of markdown and no tool calls: 17 `chat/delta` envelopes arrived between 8.0s and 19.4s and all 17 passed the channel filter, confirmed `activeTurn.responseParts.length` was 1 from 8.0s onward, and the optimistic rebase rewrote it to 0 on all 19 recomputes. The markdown observer was created at 19.4s and emitted all 2,432 characters at once.

`_promotePendingTurnStartIfTerminal` already exists because the echo can arrive without the `clientSeq`, but it fires only for `chat/turnComplete`, `chat/turnCancelled` and `chat/error`. That is why the text lands all at once at the end: the promotion happens, just not until the turn is over.

## Change

Promote the pending turn start on the first backend action naming the turn instead of only on a terminal one, and rename the method to match.

Once any backend action for a turn arrives, the server has that turn, so the optimistic start is redundant and holding it can only mask confirmed state. The body is otherwise unchanged: the start is still applied to confirmed state when the backend has not created the turn itself, so an action that arrives before any server-side `chat/turnStarted` still has a turn to land on.

Nothing changes on the origin branch, where the echo does carry the `clientSeq` and the pending action is spliced as before, and nothing changes for a chat action without a `turnId`.

## How to test

1. In a Claude agent-host session, send a prompt that produces a long reply and no tool calls, for example "without using any tools, write a numbered list from 1 to 20 with one sentence per line about database indexing".
2. Watch the response area while it runs.

The text appears incrementally as it is generated. On `main` the response area stays empty for the whole turn and the entire reply appears at once when the turn completes. Same prompt and build, before and after: 2 DOM updates becomes 13, the markdown observer is created at 7.8s instead of 19.4s, and the renderer emits 16 times across 12 seconds instead of once.

Unit coverage adds one test asserting that a `chat/responsePart` and `chat/delta` arriving while the optimistic turn start is still pending are visible in the subscription value. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.

3. Run **Reopen Editor With…** and choose **Markdown Editor**.

The Markdown editor refuses the edit, the way the text editor already does on the same staged revision.

While the file stays staged, what the editor shows is no longer what is actually staged, and nothing signals it. The file can then be committed with content that differs from what was reviewed.

title: Derive chat extension enablement from chat.disableAIFeatures
body:
chat.disableAIFeatures is registered with ConfigurationScope.WINDOW, so it is accepted in remote and workspace settings, but applying it persisted a global disable for the chat extension. That list is machine wide and shared by every window on the client, so a value set only in remote settings also disables chat in local windows, and a local window cannot recover on its own because the remote window re-applies the disable on every start.

Add EnablementState.DisabledByAIFeaturesSetting and compute it in _computeEnablementState alongside the other window-derived reasons, so the extension is disabled exactly where the setting resolves. Nothing is persisted, which makes the state follow whichever settings.json applies to the window. canChangeEnablement reports false while the setting owns the state, and a configuration listener fires onEnablementChanged so the extensions view and the extension host pick the change up.

ChatTeardownContribution no longer changes enablement. It keeps hiding the auxiliary bar and requesting the extension host restart.

Installs that already recorded the global disable would otherwise keep it forever, so the enablement service drops that entry on startup once the setting resolves to true.

title: Modern UI: Fix CSS specificity for tab action fading
body: ## Problem In Modern UI, the editor tab action fade can use the wrong color or gradient direction in some cases. This regression was introduced by #331476. ### Reproduction Configure tab actions to overlay the tab label and appear on the left: ```jsonc { "workbench.experimental.modernUI": true, "workbench.editor.tabActionLocation": "left", "workbench.editor.tabActionReserveSpace": false, "workbench.colorCustomizations": { "modernEditorTab.activeBackground": "#faa", "modernEditorTab.activeActionBackground": "#f00", "modernEditorTab.activeHoverBackground": "#ffa", "modernEditorTab.activeHoverActionBackground": "#ff0", "modernEditorTab.hoverBackground": "#afa", "modernEditorTab.hoverActionBackground": "#0f0", "tab.selectedBackground": "#aaf", "modernEditorTab.selectedActionBackground": "#00f" } } ``` Hover over or focus the editor tab actions. The fade can have the wrong color or direction. ## Fix The right-side fade previously assigned `modernEditorTab.hoverActionBackground` in a rule with higher specificity than the corresponding rules for other tab states and directions. Move the default right-side background declaration into a state-specific rule with matching specificity. This allows the active, unfocused, and left-side fade rules to override it correctly. ## Test Added unit tests for consistency of tab action background colors, fade colors, and fade directions across different tab states and locations. **Test Coverage:** - ✅ Active tab (focused and unfocused editor groups) - ✅ Hover tab (focused and unfocused editor groups) - ✅ Selected tab - ✅ Left and right tab action locations - ⚠️ Active + hover states (manual testing only) **Why active hover states are not unit tested:** The `modernEditorTab.activeHoverActionBackground` cases require a `:hover` CSS pseudo-state, which cannot be reliably simulated in unit tests. These states must be verified manually. **Manual Testing Steps:** To verify the active hover states work correctly, hover over the active tab in the following scenarios: 1. Focused editor group, tab action location on right 2. Focused editor group, tab action location on left 3. Unfocused editor group, tab action location on right 4. Unfocused editor group, tab action location on left Use the reproduction configuration from the PR description to verify the fade gradient has the correct color and direction in each case.

title: codex: surface plan updates as todo lists
body:
## Summary

- add an additive structured todo-list result to the Agent Host tool-result protocol
- map Codex `turn/plan/updated` snapshots into short-lived `update_plan` tool calls
- render those results through the workbench native todo-list surface for live and restored calls
- ignore empty snapshots and untitled plan steps

## Why

The generated Codex app-server protocol already declares `turn/plan/updated`, but `CodexAgent` does not register the notification. Plan snapshots are therefore dropped. The current AHP 1.0 tool-result union also has no structured todo content, so registering the notification alone would still produce only a generic tool card.

This change adds one provider-neutral tool-result content variant and maps it to the workbench's existing `IChatTodoListContent`. Codex statuses map as follows: `pending` → `not-started`, `inProgress` → `in-progress`, and `completed` → `completed`. The notification is routed through the owning host turn and is ignored when no host turn exists, avoiding subagent leakage.

Plan cards are live-only because Codex `thread/read` turns do not persist plan snapshots; this change does not add a persistence schema or reconstruct missing history.

## Validation

- failing baseline characterization: the focused test could not import a plan mapper from current upstream
- complete Codex mapper suite: 53 passing
- complete Agent Host state-to-progress adapter suite: 134 passing
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run typecheck-client`

title: Codex Agent Host drops turn/plan/updated notifications
body:
## Type of issue

Agent Host / Codex rendering

## Reproduction

1. Start a Codex Agent Host session.
2. Run a turn where Codex invokes `update_plan`.
3. Observe the `turn/plan/updated` app-server notification.

## Current behavior

The current generated Codex protocol includes `TurnPlanUpdatedNotification`, and the workbench already has a structured TodoList surface, but `CodexAgent` does not register `turn/plan/updated`. The notification is therefore dropped and the plan is not surfaced in the Agent Host transcript.

## Expected behavior

Map non-empty Codex plan snapshots into the existing TodoList representation on the owning host turn:

- `pending` -> `not-started`
- `inProgress` -> `in-progress`
- `completed` -> `completed`

Empty snapshots should not create cards, and child/subagent threads without a host turn must not leak plan state into the parent.

## Proposed fix

Register the notification in `CodexAgent`, add a focused mapper using the existing tool/TodoList primitives, and cover status mapping, empty snapshots, and dispatch ownership.

Codex `thread/read` does not currently retain the plan snapshot, so this would intentionally be live-only unless the upstream app-server protocol later provides persisted plan data.

title: Agent Host worktree include copying misses collapsible nested ignored directories
body:
## Type of issue

Performance / worktree creation

## Reproduction

1. Configure `git.worktreeIncludeFiles` with a glob such as `**/node_modules/**`.
2. Use a repository where a wholly ignored parent (for example `.build/`) contains both ignored files that do not match the configured glob and a large nested subtree that matches it completely, such as `.build/extensions/copilot/node_modules/**`.
3. Create an Agent Host worktree.

## Current behavior

`AgentHostGitService.copyWorktreeIncludeFiles` only collapses a directory when the entire wholly ignored root matches. If the root is only partially matched, every selected file in a fully matched nested subtree is copied as an individual entry.

In a real profile this produced 23,553 copy entries and took about 9.2 seconds.

## Expected behavior

Within a partially matched wholly ignored root, collapse the highest nested directories whose complete ignored contents match the configured globs, while preserving the existing collision checks and leaving selected files without such an ancestor as standalone entries.

A prototype reduced the same workload to 61 copy entries and about 6.0 seconds.

## Proposed fix

Extract a pure collapse helper used by `copyWorktreeIncludeFiles`, with:

- unit coverage for partially matched parents, sibling subtrees, fully matched roots, standalone files, and nested unmatched files;
- a real-Git integration test proving the copy result and progress counts;
- no protocol, configuration, or persistence changes.

title: Respect Copilot harness defaults in virtual workspaces
body:
## Summary

- honor `chat.defaultToCopilotHarness` in fully virtual workspaces when Agent Host is available
- honor `chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness` when a new virtual-workspace session would otherwise inherit Local
- preserve explicit harness choices, remembered non-Local choices, Local availability, and the Local fallback when Agent Host is unavailable
- cover default-only, preference-only, unavailable-runtime, remembered, current-session, explicit-override, and managed-sandbox behavior

## Context

This intentionally revisits the virtual-workspace precedence introduced by #326464 and #327883. That precedence unconditionally selected Local before the normal default and preference settings were evaluated. Agent Host now has client-hosted resource operations over AHP, and virtual workspaces should participate in the same rollout settings as non-virtual workspaces.

The change does not hide or disable Local in virtual workspaces. It only removes the unconditional Local short-circuit from session-type resolution, so existing availability and fallback checks remain authoritative.

title: fix: route stale AgentService.stateManager test refs through getStateManager (build fix for vscode-engineering#3678)

labels.name: vscode-build
labels.description: VS Code build process issues

body:
## Build failure

The `Compile` task on `main` failed typechecking `src/tsconfig.json` with two `TS2339` errors:

```
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts(6560,42): error TS2339: Property 'stateManager' does not exist on type 'AgentService'.
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts(6633,30): error TS2339: Property 'stateManager' does not exist on type 'AgentService'.
```

All downstream test stages cascaded from this single compile break.

## Root cause

A sealed Agent Host service graph refactor removed the public `AgentService.stateManager` escape hatch. Most call sites in `agentService.test.ts` were migrated to the `getStateManager(svc)` helper (which delegates to `getTestAgentStateManager`), but two references at lines 6560 and 6633 were left pointing at the now-removed `svc.stateManager` property, breaking the typecheck.

## How the fix works

Both stale references are updated to use the existing `getStateManager(svc)` helper already used throughout the same file. This routes through the composition-owned `AgentHostStateManager`, restoring type correctness with no behavioral change to the tests. The helper returns the same `AgentHostStateManager` whose `getSessionState` these assertions already rely on.

## Rollback evaluation

- **Recommendation:** Do not roll back.
- **Culprit:** not confirmed from public history in this environment; the source issue attributes it to the sealed Agent Host service graph refactor.
- **Rationale:** The fix is a bounded two-line test-file edit. Fix-forward is faster and safer than reverting a large service-graph refactor that later commits may depend on.
- **Owners to consult:** `@roblourens`

## Validation

Static source inspection confirms `getStateManager(svc)` returns an `AgentHostStateManager` exposing `getSessionState`, matching the surrounding usages in the same file. A full `tsgo-typecheck` build was not run in this environment; the change is confined to replacing two removed-property accesses with the established helper.

## Risk

Minimal. Change is limited to two lines in a single test file, mirroring the pattern used elsewhere in the same suite. No production code is touched.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@roblourens`

title: Add setting-gated subagent model guidance to the Copilot agent host prompt

body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in, experiment-gated setting **`chat.copilot.subagentModelGuidance.enabled`** (default `false`). When enabled, Copilot Agent Host sessions get two extra lines in the `tool_instructions` system-prompt section telling the model to keep subagents on their default model:

> When launching subagents with the task tool, leave the `model`, `reasoning_effort`, and `context_tier` parameters unset — each agent type already runs on a model suited to it, and overriding the model changes the session's cost and behavior profile.
> Only set the task tool's `model` parameter when the user explicitly names the model the subagent should run on.

When the setting is off (the default), the assembled prompt is byte-identical to today's — the committed E2E prompt baselines are unchanged.
